podcast.title: Predecessor to Primitive Radio Gods
podcast.body: The I-Rails was a Southern California band from which Primitive Radio Gods frontman Chris O'Connor evolved. Despite releasing four albums between 1985 and 1991, the band achieved no significant success and eventually broke up. "They evolved out of a Southern California band called the I-Rails, a group that amounted to exactly nothing over four albums between 1985 and 1991."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Reunion for Primitive Radio Gods Tour
podcast.body: When Primitive Radio Gods' single "Standing Outside a Broken Phone Booth with Money in My Hand" took off, singer Chris O'Connor reunited his former bandmates from The I-Rails to go on tour as Primitive Radio Gods. "When the song took off, singer Chris O'Connor got his old mates and the I-Rails back together and went on tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 2

xref.title: Solo Endeavor and Demos
xref.body: After the breakup of his previous band, The I-Rails, singer Chris O'Connor began recording Public Enemy-inspired material under the name Primitive Radio Gods. He initially received no interest from radio or the music industry for these demos and decided to retire from music in 1994. "The band broke up, and singer Chris O'Connor went out on his own, recording some public enemy-inspired material under the name Primitive Radio Gods."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
